🚨 ANOTHER DEVELOPMENT IN THE 9/11 DECLAS TIMELINE

And this one comes just DAYS before the 25th anniversary of September 11th.

We recently added a major development to our growing 9/11 timeline:

⚖️ A military judge threw out Khalid Sheikh Mohammed’s crucial 2007 FBI confession, ruling that prosecutors failed to establish that the statements were voluntary following years of CIA detention and coercive interrogation. (CBS News)

Now there’s another development.

🇺🇸 THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT APPEALING.

Military prosecutors have decided they will NOT attempt to reinstate KSM’s confession and instead intend to proceed toward his military-commission trial without it. (GV Wire)

Why?

According to the prosecution team’s communication to victims’ families:

An appeal could jeopardize the June 5, 2028 trial date. (WHMI Radio)

Think about the significance of the sequence.

🔹 After more than two decades of legal paralysis, KSM and three co-defendants finally receive a firm military trial date.

🔹 Days later, the military judge excludes what prosecutors had regarded as a crucial confession.

🔹 Rather than launching another potentially years-long appellate battle, prosecutors abandon their effort to use that confession.

🔹 They will instead move toward trial using the government’s remaining evidence, reportedly including financial records and phone records connecting KSM to the plot. (New York Post)

And all of this is happening as we approach the 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF 9/11.

That’s why I’m adding this as another entry in the 9/11 DECLAS / CONVERGENCE TIMELINE we’ve been tracking.

The important takeaway isn’t that this proves anything about what the eventual trial will reveal.

It’s that after YEARS of delays, plea-deal battles, suppressed evidence, appeals and litigation, the government has now made a consequential choice:

⚖️ KEEP THE MILITARY TRIAL MOVING — EVEN WITHOUT KSM’S CONFESSION.

Another piece moves into place.
